contentHtml:
tempura chicken nuggets whisk you to a breezy street festival, each golden bite crackling with playful energy. Tender chicken pieces dip into a light, bubbly batter made with a splash of sparkling water and a pinch of sea salt, then fry up ultra crisp outside and juicy inside. Swirl them through a tangy soy-ginger sauce for lively contrast, or pair with spicy mayo for extra kick. Perfect for a cozy movie night or a cheerful gathering, this easy recipe turns simple pantry staples into a fun, mess-friendly cooking adventure that disappears fast.

Why You’ll Love This tempura chicken nuggets

  • Deliciously crispy texture that’s hard to resist.
  • Quick and easy to make for busy weeknights.
  • Perfectly seasoned for a burst of flavor in every bite.
  • Great for dipping in your favorite sauces.
  • A fun twist on traditional chicken nuggets that everyone will love!

tempura chicken nuggets

Discover the ultimate crispy tempura chicken nuggets recipe! Easy to make and deliciously addictive, these Japanese-style bites are a must-try! 🍗✨
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 15 minutes mins
Cook Time 10 minutes mins
Total Time 25 minutes mins
Servings: 4 servings
Course: Appetizer
Cuisine: Japanese
Calories: 300
Ingredients Equipment Method Notes

Ingredients
  

Chicken
  • 2 breasts boneless, skinless chicken Cut into bite-sized pieces
Batter
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour For the coating
  • 1/2 cup corn starch Adds crispiness
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder Helps with fluffiness
  • 1 teaspoon salt Enhances flavor
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper For a little kick
  • 1 large egg Binds the batter
  • 3/4 cup ice-cold water Helps create a light batter
  • Vegetable oil for frying
  • Optional dipping sauce Soy sauce, sweet chili sauce, or tempura dipping sauce

Equipment

  • 1 Deep pot or fryer For frying the chicken nuggets
  • 1 whisk For mixing the batter
  • 1 Slotted Spoon For transferring cooked nuggets
  • 1 Paper towels For draining excess oil

Method
 

Preparation
  1. Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season them lightly with salt and pepper. This helps the batter stick better!
Batter Preparation
  1. In a bowl, whisk together flour, corn starch, baking powder, and salt. In a separate bowl, beat the egg and mix it with ice-cold water. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir lightly. Remember, the batter should be lumpy and cold!
Heating Oil
  1. Pour vegetable oil into a deep pot or fryer to a depth of 2–3 inches. Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C). This is the perfect temperature for frying!
Coating and Frying
  1. Dip each chicken piece into the batter, letting the excess drip off. Carefully lower them into the hot oil. Fry in batches for 3–4 minutes, or until they are golden and crispy. Yum!
Draining
  1. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the cooked nuggets to a paper towel–lined plate. This will help drain the excess oil and keep them crispy!
Serving
  1. Serve your tempura chicken nuggets hot with your favorite dipping sauce. Enjoy every crunchy bite!

How to Make tempura chicken nuggets

Get ready to enjoy some crispy tempura chicken nuggets! This delightful recipe takes about 15 minutes to prepare and 10 minutes to cook. You’ll want to serve them hot, so have your favorite dipping sauce ready!

Step 1: Prepare chicken

Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season them lightly with salt and pepper. This helps the batter stick better!

Step 2: Make batter

In a bowl, whisk together flour, corn starch, baking powder, and salt. In a separate bowl, beat the egg and mix it with ice-cold water. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir lightly. Remember, the batter should be lumpy and cold!

Step 3: Heat oil

Pour vegetable oil into a deep pot or fryer to a depth of 2–3 inches. Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C). This is the perfect temperature for frying!

Step 4: Coat and fry

Dip each chicken piece into the batter, letting the excess drip off. Carefully lower them into the hot oil. Fry in batches for 3–4 minutes, or until they are golden and crispy. Yum!

Step 5: Drain

Using a slotted spoon, transfer the cooked nuggets to a paper towel–lined plate. This will help drain the excess oil and keep them crispy!

Step 6: Serve

Serve your tempura chicken nuggets hot with your favorite dipping sauce. Enjoy every crunchy bite!

Recipe Snapshot

Pro Tips for Making tempura chicken nuggets

  • Use ice-cold water for the batter to achieve that perfect crispiness.
  • Don’t overcrowd the frying pan; fry in batches for even cooking.
  • Pat the chicken dry before coating to help the batter stick better.
  • Experiment with different seasonings in the batter for unique flavors.
  • Serve immediately for the best texture and taste.

How to Serve this tempura chicken nuggets

  • Serve with a side of sweet chili sauce for a delightful dip.
  • Pair with a fresh cucumber salad for a refreshing crunch.
  • Enjoy alongside steamed rice or sushi rice for a complete meal.
  • Top with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and chopped green onions for added flavor.
  • Try them in a wrap with lettuce and your favorite sauce for a fun twist.
  • Serve with a side of miso soup for a cozy Japanese-inspired dinner.

Make Ahead and Storage

Here’s how to keep your tempura chicken nuggets fresh and delicious:

Storing Leftovers

  • Allow nuggets to cool completely.
  • Place in an airtight container.
  • Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

Freezing

  • Cool nuggets completely before freezing.
  • Arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet.
  • Freeze until solid, then transfer to a freezer bag.
  • Label and store for up to 2 months.

Reheating

  • Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
  • Place nuggets on a baking sheet in a single layer.
  • Bake for 10-15 minutes until heated through.
  • For extra crispiness, broil for 1-2 minutes at the end.

FAQs

Here’s a helpful FAQ about this recipe:

1. What are Chicken Nuggets tempura?

Tempura chicken nuggets are a delightful twist on traditional chicken nuggets, featuring a light and crispy batter made from a tempura-style mixture. This Japanese cooking technique involves coating the chicken pieces in a batter made from flour and cold water, then frying them quickly to achieve a crunchy exterior while keeping the inside tender and juicy. They are perfect for dipping and make a fantastic appetizer or snack!

2. What is the difference between tempura nuggets and normal nuggets?

The main difference lies in the batter and cooking method. Tempura nuggets are coated in a light, airy batter that is typically made with cold water and flour, resulting in a crispier texture. In contrast, traditional chicken nuggets are usually breaded with breadcrumbs or a thicker batter, which can be denser. Tempura nuggets also tend to have a lighter flavor, allowing the taste of the chicken to shine through more than in regular nuggets.

3. Is McDonald’s chicken nugget tempura?

No, McDonald’s chicken nuggets are not tempura. They are made with a breaded coating that is thicker and denser than the light batter used in tempura. McDonald’s nuggets are designed to be crispy but have a different texture and flavor profile compared to traditional tempura chicken nuggets, which are lighter and airier.

4. What are tempura chicken bites?

Tempura chicken bites are small pieces of chicken that are coated in a tempura batter and fried until golden and crispy. They are similar to tempura chicken nuggets but are often cut into bite-sized pieces, making them perfect for snacking or sharing. These bites are typically served with dipping sauces, enhancing their flavor and making them a popular choice for appetizers or party platters.

Final Thoughts

Now that you have the recipe for these delightful tempura chicken nuggets, it’s time to gather your loved ones and enjoy! They’re crispy, fun to make, and oh-so-satisfying. Remember, cooking is all about joy and sharing, so dive in and savor every bite. Happy cooking!
